issues.description: Class property Course.instructor has inconsistent types across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly describes Course.instructor as a String and the template (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift) declares `let instructor: String` (template line shows the instructor property). In the solution implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift) the property is declared as `let instructor: [String]` and the initializer signature uses `instructor: [String]`. Additionally, the solution's Client (Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift) constructs a Course passing a single String for the instructor argument ("Matthias, Patrick, and Felix"), which contradicts the solution's instructor type and would cause a compilation/type error. This mismatch will confuse students about the expected type for the instructor parameter and may break compilation of the solution or student code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the instructor type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem statement and template by using a single String for instructor (update Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift to `let instructor: String` and the initializer to `init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int])`, and adjust any usages). Alternatively, if multiple instructors are intended, update the problem statement, template, and Client example to document and pass an array of Strings (e.g. ["Matthias", "Patrick", "Felix"]) and change all initializer call sites to provide [String]. Ensure all three artifacts (problem statement, template, and solution including Client) use the same type.
